items.title: Lew Tabackin interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: He did a Charlie Parker, “Little Suede Shoes,” whatever. ... What did Charlie Parker say? ... He said, “Well you bite down as hard as you can on the mouthpiece...”

ctx.x: Can you remember the kind of jazz you were hearing early on then?

Well the first stuff I heard was, well since I played flute, a friend next door, he played me some stuff with Milt Jackson, Frank Wess, you know those things, “Opus de Funk” those kind of — I said wow that’s nice. And Herbie Mann had a hit record or something. He did a Charlie Parker, “Little Suede Shoes,” whatever. Anything I had was very unsophisticated, and then I would just try to play. I didn’t know what I was playing, but it was exciting. Because you never can quite recapture the exuberance of being totally…
